subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw core verify or fail closed on Telegram/ACP visible success claims when the same turn lacks matching tool-result evidence, or should generic claim verification remain plugin/ClawHub-owned?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves private final text in message-tool-only mode and only logs a narrow stranded-final warning; expanding that to arbitrary side-effect claims changes channel UX, privacy, fallback, and plugin/core ownership policy.

options.title: Define a core invariant
options.body: Make externally sourced Telegram/ACP success claims require structured tool-result evidence or an explicit diagnostic/failure outcome before visible delivery.

options.title: Keep claim verification plugin-owned
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core limited to delivery evidence and diagnostics, and direct generic success-claim verification to ClawHub/plugin implementations.

options.title: Split by failure class
options.body: Let the stranded-final PR handle missing message-tool delivery while keeping this issue open only for a narrower Telegram/ACP live repro of unsupported success claims.

recommendation.title: Define a core invariant
recommendation.body: Make externally sourced Telegram/ACP success claims require structured tool-result evidence or an explicit diagnostic/failure outcome before visible delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest product-boundary signal from PR 86463 and the ClawHub/plugin-scope decision on the related claim-verification issue.
